        lines.append(f"| {i} | {str(a.get('created_at', ''))[:16]} | {frm} → {a['to_state']} | {a['action']} | "
                     f"{cell((a.get('payload') or {}).get('actor_role', 'system'))} |")
    if audit:
        lines.append(f"\nChain head: `{audit[-1]['hash']}`")
    lines += ["", "<details><summary>Structured cleanup patch</summary>", "", "```json",
              json.dumps(patch, indent=2, default=str), "```", "</details>"]
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Open the cleanup PR: live GitHub REST API (Git Data API, one commit) or the sandbox provider.

Live sequence (GITHUB_CLEANUP_TOKEN, fine-grained: Contents RW + Pull requests RW on SUNSET_CLEANUP_REPO
only; the ingest token stays read-only):

    GET  /repos/{repo}                              default branch (unless SUNSET_CLEANUP_BASE)
    GET  /repos/{repo}/git/ref/heads/{base}         base commit
    GET  /repos/{repo}/git/commits/{sha}            base tree
    GET  /repos/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}?recursive=1 files that actually exist (deletions are intersected)
    GET  /repos/{repo}/contents/features.yaml       manifest as committed on the base branch
    POST /repos/{repo}/git/trees                    deletions (sha: null) + manifest edit + cleanup patch
    POST /repos/{repo}/git/commits                  one commit, parent = base
    POST /repos/{repo}/git/refs                     sunset/<feature_key>  (exists -> PATCH force)
    POST /repos/{repo}/pulls                        the PR (exists -> reuse the open one, refresh body)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

from ..config import config
from ..connectors.base import Transport
from .change import CleanupChange


class CleanupProviderError(RuntimeError):

@dataclass
class CleanupPR:
    provider: str
    repo: str
    number: int
    url: str | None
    branch: str
    base_branch: str
    head_sha: str | None
    files_deleted: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    files_edited: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


class CleanupPRProvider(Protocol):

    repo: str

    async def list_files(self) -> list[str] | None: ...
    async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None: ...
    async def open_pr(self, change: CleanupChange, *, next_number: int) -> CleanupPR: ...

def _ok(r, what: str, allow: tuple[int, ...] = ()) -> Any:
    if r.status >= 400 and r.status not in allow:
        msg = r.body.get("message") if isinstance(r.body, dict) else str(r.body)[:200]
        raise CleanupProviderError(f"GitHub {what} failed: HTTP {r.status} {msg}")
    return r.body


class GitHubCleanupProvider:
    name = "github"

    def __init__(self, transport: Transport, repo: str, base: str | None = None):
        self.t, self.repo, self.base = transport, repo, base
        self._base_sha: str | None = None
        self._tree_sha: str | None = None
        self._files: list[str] | None = None

    async def _resolve_base(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        if not self.base:
            self.base = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}"), "read repo")["default_branch"]
        if not self._base_sha:
            ref = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/ref/heads/{self.base}"), "read base ref")
            self._base_sha = ref["object"]["sha"]
            commit = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/commits/{self._base_sha}"), "read commit")
            self._tree_sha = commit["tree"]["sha"]
        return self.base, self._base_sha, self._tree_sha  # type: ignore[return-value]

    async def list_files(self) -> list[str] | None:
        _, _, tree = await self._resolve_base()
        body = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/trees/{tree}", params={"recursive": "1"}),
                   "list tree")
        if body.get("truncated"):
            return None
        self._files = [e["path"] for e in body.get("tree", []) if e.get("type") == "blob"]
        return self._files

    async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        base, _, _ = await self._resolve_base()
        r = await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/contents/{path}", params={"ref": base})
        if r.status == 404:
            return None
        body = _ok(r, f"read {path}")
        return base64.b64decode(body.get("content", "")).decode()

async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        base, _, _ = await self._resolve_base()
        r = await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/contents/{path}", params={"ref": base})
        if r.status == 404:
            return None
        body = _ok(r, f"read {path}")
        return base64.b64decode(body.get("content", "")).decode()

    async def open_pr(self, change: CleanupChange, *, next_number: int = 0) -> CleanupPR:
        base, base_sha, tree_sha = await self._resolve_base()
        deletions = [p for p in change.deletions if self._files is None or p in set(self._files)]
        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"path": p, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "sha": None} for p in deletions]
        if change.manifest_after is not None:
            entries.append({"path": change.manifest_path, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob",
                            "content": change.manifest_after})
        entries.append({"path": change.patch_path, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob",
                        "content": json.dumps(change.patch, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"})
        tree = _ok(await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/trees",
                                        json_body={"base_tree": tree_sha, "tree": entries}), "create tree")
        commit = _ok(await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/commits", json_body={
            "message": f"{change.title}\n\nAutomated by FeatureLedger Safe Sunset (plan {change.patch['plan_id']}).",
            "tree": tree["sha"], "parents": [base_sha]}), "create commit")
        r = await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/refs",
                                 json_body={"ref": f"refs/heads/{change.branch}", "sha": commit["sha"]})
        if r.status == 422:   # branch left over from an earlier attempt: move it to the new commit
            _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/refs/heads/{change.branch}",
                                     json_body={"sha": commit["sha"], "force": True}), "update branch")
        else:
            _ok(r, "create branch")
        r = await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls", json_body={
            "title": change.title, "head": change.branch, "base": base, "body": change.body,
            "maintainer_can_modify": True})
        if r.status == 422:
            owner = self.repo.split("/")[0]
            existing = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls",
                                                params={"head": f"{owner}:{change.branch}", "state": "open"}),
                           "find existing PR")
            if not existing:
                _ok(r, "open PR")
            pr = existing[0]
            _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls/{pr['number']}",
                                     json_body={"title": change.title, "body": change.body}), "refresh PR")
        else:
            pr = _ok(r, "open PR")
        await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/issues/{pr['number']}/labels",
                             json_body={"labels": ["featureledger-sunset"]})   # best effort
        return CleanupPR("github", self.repo, int(pr["number"]), pr.get("html_url"), change.branch, base,
                         commit["sha"], deletions, change.files_edited + [change.patch_path])

    async def close_pr(self, number: int, comment: str) -> None:
        await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/issues/{number}/comments", json_body={"body": comment})
        _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls/{number}", json_body={"state": "closed"}),
            "close PR")

class SandboxGitHubProvider:
    """Records the PR it would open (same CleanupChange as live) without a network call. A PR merge is
    simulated by POSTing a GitHub-shaped `pull_request` webhook to the real webhook endpoint."""
    name = "sandbox"

    def __init__(self, repo: str = "northwind/app", base: str = "main"):
        self.repo, self.base = repo, base
        self.opened: list[CleanupChange] = []
        self.closed: list[int] = []

    async def list_files(self) -> list[str] | None:
        return None   # use the files FeatureLedger has seen in merged PRs and import edges

    async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        return None   # use the active manifest version

    async def open_pr(self, change: CleanupChange, *, next_number: int = 1001) -> CleanupPR:
        self.opened.append(change)
        sha = hashlib.sha1((change.body + change.branch).encode()).hexdigest()
        return CleanupPR("sandbox", self.repo, next_number, None, change.branch, self.base, sha,
                         list(change.deletions), change.files_edited + [change.patch_path])

    async def close_pr(self, number: int, comment: str) -> None:
        self.closed.append(number)


_override: CleanupPRProvider | None = None


def set_cleanup_provider(p: CleanupPRProvider | None) -> None:
    global _override
    _override = p


def get_cleanup_provider() -> CleanupPRProvider:
    if _override is not None:
        return _override
    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_CLEANUP_TOKEN")
    if token and config.cleanup_repo:
        from ..connectors.http import HttpxTransport
        t = HttpxTransport("https://api.github.com", headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
            "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28", "User-Agent": "featureledger-sunset"})
        return GitHubCleanupProvider(t, config.cleanup_repo, config.cleanup_base_branch)
    if config.sandbox_mode:
        return SandboxGitHubProvider(config.cleanup_repo or "northwind/app", config.cleanup_base_branch or "main")
    raise CleanupProviderError("set SUNSET_CLEANUP_REPO and GITHUB_CLEANUP_TOKEN (Contents + Pull requests: "
                               "read & write on that repo) to open cleanup PRs")

"""AWS Cost Explorer: monthly UnblendedCost grouped by the `feature` cost-allocation tag and SERVICE.

Cost Explorer is not plain REST (SigV4, JSON-RPC), so this connector talks to a `CostExplorerApi`:
the live one wraps boto3 (run in a thread, behind the same token bucket), the sandbox one serves fixtures.
Months are restated by AWS for a few days after month end, so incremental syncs always re-read the
previous and current month; the processor rebuilds a month from the latest envelopes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import date
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Protocol

from .base import Batch, Connector, SyncCtx, add_months, month_start

LLM_SERVICES = {"Amazon Bedrock", "Amazon SageMaker", "Claude (Amazon Bedrock Edition)"}


class CostExplorerApi(Protocol):
    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


class Boto3CostExplorer:
    def __init__(self, region: str, limiter=None):
        import boto3  # only needed in live mode
        self._ce = boto3.client("ce", region_name=region)
        self._limiter = limiter

    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if self._limiter:
            await self._limiter()
        return await asyncio.to_thread(self._ce.get_cost_and_usage, **kwargs)


def split_tag(key: str, tag: str) -> str | None:
    """CE returns 'feature$legacy-pdf-export' (or 'feature$' when untagged)."""
    prefix = f"{tag}$"
    v = key[len(prefix):] if key.startswith(prefix) else key
    return v or None


def cost_type_for(service: str) -> str:
    return "llm" if service in LLM_SERVICES else "infra"


class AwsCostExplorerConnector(Connector):
    kind = "aws_cost_explorer"
    streams = ("costs",)

    def __init__(self, api: CostExplorerApi, tag_key: str = "feature"):
        super().__init__(transport=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        self.api = api
        self.tag = tag_key

kind = "aws_cost_explorer"
    streams = ("costs",)

    def __init__(self, api: CostExplorerApi, tag_key: str = "feature"):
        super().__init__(transport=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        self.api = api
        self.tag = tag_key

    async def _month(self, ctx: SyncCtx, m: date) -> Batch:
        envs, token = [], None
        while True:
            kw: dict[str, Any] = {
                "TimePeriod": {"Start": m.isoformat(), "End": add_months(m, 1).isoformat()},
                "Granularity": "MONTHLY", "Metrics": ["UnblendedCost"],
                "GroupBy": [{"Type": "TAG", "Key": self.tag}, {"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "SERVICE"}],
            }
            if token:
                kw["NextPageToken"] = token
            r = await self.api.get_cost_and_usage(**kw)
            for period in r.get("ResultsByTime", []):
                for g in period.get("Groups", []):
                    tag_key, service = g["Keys"][0], g["Keys"][1]
                    amt = round(float(g["Metrics"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"]), 4)
                    p = {"month": m.isoformat(), "feature_tag": split_tag(tag_key, self.tag), "service": service,
                         "cost_type": cost_type_for(service), "amount_usd": amt,
                         "unit": g["Metrics"]["UnblendedCost"].get("Unit", "USD")}
                    envs.append(ctx.envelope("aws_cost", f"{m.isoformat()}|{p['feature_tag'] or ''}|{service}",
                                             str(amt), p))
            token = r.get("NextPageToken")
            if not token:
                return Batch("costs", envs, m.isoformat())

    async def backfill(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        now = month_start(ctx.now())
        m = add_months(now, -ctx.backfill_months)
        while m <= now:
            yield await self._month(ctx, m)
            m = add_months(m, 1)

    async def incremental(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str, cursor: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        now = month_start(ctx.now())
        m = min(add_months(now, -1), date.fromisoformat(cursor[:10]))
        while m <= now:
            yield await self._month(ctx, m)
            m = add_months(m, 1)

"""The unified connector contract (spec §3.1).

A connector is a set of *streams* (Jira issues, Stripe invoices, PostHog monthly usage...). Each stream
is read either as a backfill (no cursor yet) or incrementally (from its stored cursor) and yields
`Batch`es. The runner commits a batch's envelopes to `ingest_inbox` and advances the stream's cursor in
the SAME transaction, so a crash can replay a batch but never skip one.

Connectors are pure with respect to storage: they only talk to a `Transport` (live HTTP or sandbox
fixtures) and emit scrubbed, idempotent `Envelope`s. Normalization into canonical tables happens later,
in `processors.py`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Callable, Protocol


class NotConfigured(RuntimeError):
    """Credentials or settings for a live connector are missing."""


class HttpError(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self, status: int, url: str, body: Any = None):
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status} for {url}")
        self.status = status
        self.url = url
        self.body = body


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HttpResponse:
    status: int
    headers: dict[str, str]
    body: Any


class Transport(Protocol):
    async def request(self, method: str, url: str, *, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
                      json_body: Any = None, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> HttpResponse: ...


def content_hash(obj: Any) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

def add_months(m: date, n: int) -> date:
    y, mo = divmod(m.month - 1 + n, 12)
    return date(m.year + y, mo + 1, 1)


class Connector:
    """Base class. Subclasses set `kind` and `streams`, and implement `backfill` and `incremental`."""

    kind: str = ""
    streams: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __init__(self, transport: Transport):
        self.t = transport

    async def backfill(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        raise NotImplementedError
        yield  # pragma: no cover

    async def incremental(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str, cursor: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        raise NotImplementedError
        yield  # pragma: no cover

    def handle_webhook(self, ctx: SyncCtx, headers: dict[str, str], body: bytes) -> list[Envelope]:
        """Turn a verified webhook into envelopes. Default: none (the webhook only triggers a sync)."""
        return []

    async def sync(self, ctx: SyncCtx, cursors: dict[str, str]) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        for stream in self.streams:
            cur = cursors.get(stream)
            it = self.incremental(ctx, stream, cur) if cur else self.backfill(ctx, stream)
            async for batch in it:
                yield batch

"""Live HTTP transport (httpx). Imported lazily so the pure connector code needs no network stack."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from .base import HttpResponse


class HttpxTransport:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None, auth: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
                 timeout: float = 30.0):
        import httpx
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=base_url, headers=headers or {}, auth=auth, timeout=timeout,
                                         follow_redirects=False)

    async def request(self, method: str, url: str, *, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None, json_body: Any = None,
                      headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> HttpResponse:
        r = await self._client.request(method, url, params=params, json=json_body, headers=headers)
        try:
            body = r.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = r.text
        return HttpResponse(r.status_code, dict(r.headers), body)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._client.aclose()

def stripe_accounts(customers: list[dict], subs: list[dict], invoices: list[dict],
                    fx: dict[str, float]) -> list[StripeAccount]:
    subs_by: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    inv_by: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    for s in subs:
        subs_by[s["customer"]].append(s)
    for i in invoices:
        inv_by[i["customer"]].append(i)
    out = []
    for c in customers:
        if c.get("deleted"):

        st = account_state(c, subs_by.get(c["id"], []), fx)
        mrr = monthly_mrr_from_invoices(inv_by.get(c["id"], []), fx)
        out.append(StripeAccount(
            c["id"], c["name"], c.get("email_domain") or (c.get("metadata") or {}).get("domain"), st["plan_tier"],
            st["arr_usd"], date.fromisoformat(st["renewal_date"]) if st["renewal_date"] else None, st["health"],
            st["csm_email"], {m: round(v * 12, 2) for m, v in mrr.items()}))
    return out

"""PostHog (Query API + Groups API), B2B usage at the tenant (group) level.

Streams
  `groups` : GET /api/projects/{id}/groups/?group_type_index=N  (paged by `next`), full refresh each run.
  `usage`  : POST /api/projects/{id}/query with two HogQL queries per calendar month:
               per (group, event): distinct active days, distinct persons, event count
               per group:          distinct active days across all events (the concentration denominator)
             Backfill: the last `backfill_months` complete months + the current one. Incremental: the
             previous month (late events) + the current one. Cursor = last month fully read.
Only aggregates leave PostHog: no person ids, no properties other than the group's name and domain.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator

from .base import Batch, Connector, SyncCtx, add_months, content_hash, month_start
from .scrub import scrub_posthog_group

USAGE_HOGQL = """
SELECT {group_col} AS group_key, event,
       count(DISTINCT toDate(timestamp)) AS active_days,
       count(DISTINCT person_id) AS active_users,
       count() AS events
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= {start} AND timestamp < {end} AND {group_col} != ''
GROUP BY group_key, event
ORDER BY group_key, event
LIMIT 500000
"""
ACTIVITY_HOGQL = """
SELECT {group_col} AS group_key, count(DISTINCT toDate(timestamp)) AS active_days
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= {start} AND timestamp < {end} AND {group_col} != ''
GROUP BY group_key
LIMIT 500000
"""


class PostHogConnector(Connector):
    kind = "posthog"
    streams = ("groups", "usage")

    def __init__(self, transport, project_id: str, group_type_index: int = 0):
        super().__init__(transport)
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.gti = group_type_index
        self.group_col = f"$group_{group_type_index}"

"""Inbox processors: pending envelopes -> canonical tables, in bulk, with dead-letter isolation.

Run inside an org-scoped transaction. Order matters (accounts before anything that stitches to them):
  stripe_customer/subscription/invoice -> zendesk_org, posthog_group (stitching) -> jira_issue ->
  zendesk_ticket -> posthog_usage/activity (month rebuild) -> aws_cost (month rebuild)

Isolation: a payload that fails to normalize fails alone. A handler whose SQL fails is rolled back to its
savepoint and all of its envelopes are marked failed. Every failure increments `attempts`; at 5 the
envelope is dead-lettered (`dead_lettered_at`) and never blocks its stream again. The Sync Health view
lists dead letters and can re-queue them.

Rebuild-style sources (Stripe accounts, PostHog months, AWS months) recompute their output from the
LATEST version of every envelope of that entity, so replays and restatements converge.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from ..core.manifest import Manifest
from . import normalize as N
from .stitching import UNRESOLVED_REF, AccountIndex

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.processors")
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
ORDER = ["stripe_customer", "stripe_subscription", "stripe_invoice", "zendesk_org", "posthog_group", "jira_issue",
         "zendesk_ticket", "posthog_usage", "posthog_activity", "aws_cost"]
TICKET_NS = uuid.UUID("0d1c9f3e-2b7a-4c55-9a51-6c1f0e2d8b44")

LATEST_SQL = """SELECT DISTINCT ON (external_id) external_id, payload FROM ingest_inbox
                 WHERE entity_type = $1 AND {cond} ORDER BY external_id, received_at DESC"""


@dataclass
class Stats:
    processed: int = 0
    failed: int = 0
    dead_lettered: int = 0
    accounts_upserted: int = 0
    months_rebuilt: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    unresolved_groups: int = 0
    unknown_events: int = 0
    unmatched_orgs: int = 0

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return dict(self.__dict__)


async def _latest(conn, entity: str, cond: str, *args) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [r["payload"] for r in await conn.fetch(LATEST_SQL.format(cond=cond), entity, *args)]

async def _stitch(conn, org_id: str, index: AccountIndex, kind: str, payloads: list[dict], st: Stats) -> None:
    if kind == "posthog":
        matches = N.group_matches(payloads, index)

    st = Stats()
    pending = await conn.fetch("""
        SELECT idempotency_key, entity_type, external_id, payload, attempts FROM ingest_inbox
         WHERE processed_at IS NULL AND dead_lettered_at IS NULL ORDER BY received_at LIMIT $1""", limit)
    by_type: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)

        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001

"""Try to take `cost` tokens. Returns 0 on success, else seconds to wait before retrying."""


@dataclass
class MemoryBucketStore:
    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    state: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    async def take(self, key: str, rate: float, capacity: int, cost: float = 1.0) -> float:
        now = self.clock()
        tokens, ts = self.state.get(key, (float(capacity), now))
        tokens = min(float(capacity), tokens + (now - ts) * rate)
        if tokens >= cost:
            self.state[key] = (tokens - cost, now)
            return 0.0
        self.state[key] = (tokens, now)
        return (cost - tokens) / rate


TAKE_LUA = """
local cap = tonumber(ARGV[1]); local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2]); local now = tonumber(ARGV[3]); local cost = tonumber(ARGV[4])
local b = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', 'ts')
local tokens = tonumber(b[1]) or cap
local ts = tonumber(b[2]) or now
tokens = math.min(cap, tokens + math.max(now - ts, 0) * rate)
local wait = 0
if tokens >= cost then tokens = tokens - cost else wait = (cost - tokens) / rate end
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tokens, 'ts', now)
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], 3600)
return tostring(wait)
"""


class RedisBucketStore:
    """Shared across worker processes, so N workers never exceed one vendor limit together."""

    def __init__(self, redis: Any):
        self.redis = redis

    async def take(self, key: str, rate: float, capacity: int, cost: float = 1.0) -> float:
        wait = await self.redis.eval(TAKE_LUA, 1, f"fl:bucket:{key}", capacity, rate, time.time(), cost)
        return float(wait.decode() if isinstance(wait, bytes) else wait)


class RetryingTransport:
    def __init__(self, inner: Transport, store: BucketStore, bucket_key: str, rate: float, capacity: int,
                 max_attempts: int = 6, sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep,
                 rng: random.Random | None = None):
        self.inner, self.store, self.key = inner, store, bucket_key
        self.rate, self.capacity, self.max_attempts = rate, capacity, max_attempts
        self.sleep, self.rng = sleep, rng
        self.stats = {"requests": 0, "throttled_waits": 0, "retries": 0}

Used by the ARQ worker (scheduled, manual and webhook-triggered syncs). `tx` is an org-scoped
transaction factory (app.db.org_tx in production), injectable for tests.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging

from ..config import config

from ..graph.manifest_store import active_manifest

INSERT_ENVELOPE = """
    INSERT INTO ingest_inbox (idempotency_key, org_id, integration_id, entity_type, external_id, external_version, payload)
    VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7) ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING"""


async def write_envelopes(conn, org_id: str, envelopes: list[Envelope]) -> int:
    if not envelopes:
        return 0
    before = await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM ingest_inbox WHERE idempotency_key = ANY($1)",
                                 [e.idempotency_key for e in envelopes])
    await conn.executemany(INSERT_ENVELOPE, [(e.idempotency_key, org_id, e.integration_id, e.entity_type, e.external_id,
                                              e.external_version, e.payload) for e in envelopes])
    return len({e.idempotency_key for e in envelopes}) - int(before)


async def commit_batch(conn, org_id: str, integration_id: str, batch: Batch) -> int:
    """Envelopes and the stream cursor in ONE transaction: a crash replays a batch, never skips one."""
    new = await write_envelopes(conn, org_id, batch.envelopes)
    if batch.cursor:
        await conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO sync_cursors (integration_id, org_id, entity_type, cursor) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
            ON CONFLICT (integration_id, entity_type) DO UPDATE SET cursor = EXCLUDED.cursor, updated_at = now()""",
            integration_id, org_id, batch.stream, batch.cursor)
    return new

async def run_integration(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, integ: dict[str, Any], trigger: str,
                          store: BucketStore, manifest_text: str, vault: TextVault | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    iid = str(integ["id"])
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        run_id = await conn.fetchval("""INSERT INTO sync_runs (org_id, integration_id, trigger) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
                                        RETURNING id""", org_id, iid, trigger)
        cursors = {r["entity_type"]: str(r["cursor"]) for r in await conn.fetch(
            "SELECT entity_type, cursor FROM sync_cursors WHERE integration_id = $1", iid)}
    res = {"run_id": run_id, "kind": integ["kind"], "batches": 0, "seen": 0, "new": 0, "status": "succeeded",
           "error": None}
    try:
        built = build(integ["kind"], org_id, iid, integ.get("config") or {}, bool(integ.get("sandbox")), store,
                      manifest_text)
    except NotConfigured as e:
        res.update(status="failed", error=str(e))
        async with tx(org_id) as conn:
            await _finish(conn, res)
            await conn.execute("UPDATE integrations SET status = 'pending', last_error = $2 WHERE id = $1", iid, str(e))
        return res
    try:
        async for batch in built.connector.sync(built.ctx, cursors):
            async with tx(org_id) as conn:
                res["new"] += await commit_batch(conn, org_id, iid, batch)
            if vault is not None:   # raw text for Tier 3 stays in memory; only payloads were written above
                for e in batch.envelopes:
                    if e.ephemeral_text:
                        vault.put(e.entity_type, e.external_id, e.ephemeral_text)
            res["batches"] += 1
            res["seen"] += len(batch.envelopes)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - recorded on the run; committed batches stay committed
        log.exception("sync %s failed", integ["kind"])
        res.update(status="partial" if res["batches"] else "failed", error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:500])
    finally:
        await built.close()
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        await _finish(conn, res)
        if res["status"] == "succeeded":
            await conn.execute("""UPDATE integrations SET status = 'active', last_error = NULL, last_synced_at = now()
                                  WHERE id = $1""", iid)
        else:
            await conn.execute("UPDATE integrations SET status = 'error', last_error = $2 WHERE id = $1", iid,
                               res["error"])
    return res

    await conn.execute("""UPDATE sync_runs SET status = $2::sync_status, finished_at = now(), batches = $3,
                          envelopes_seen = $4, envelopes_new = $5, error = $6 WHERE id = $1""",
                       res["run_id"], res["status"], res["batches"], res["seen"], res["new"], res["error"])

async def process_org(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, run_ids: list[int] | None = None) -> Stats:
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        manifest = await active_manifest(conn)
        st = await process_inbox(conn, org_id, manifest, fx_rates())
        if run_ids:
            await conn.execute("UPDATE sync_runs SET processed = $2, dead_lettered = $3 WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[])",
                               run_ids, st.processed, st.dead_lettered)
    return st


async def sync_org(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, integrations: list[dict[str, Any]], trigger: str,
                   store: BucketStore, recompute: Callable[[str], Awaitable[Any]] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Sync the given integrations in dependency order, then process the inbox, then recompute the P&L."""
    manifest_text = config.manifest_path.read_text()   # sandbox fixtures are built from the shipped manifest
    order = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(SYNC_ORDER)}
    results = []
    vault = TextVault()
    try:
        for integ in sorted(integrations, key=lambda i: order.get(i["kind"], 99)):
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            results.append(await run_integration(tx, org_id, integ, trigger, store, manifest_text, vault))
            log.info("sync %s: %s %s in %.1fs", org_id, integ["kind"], results[-1]["status"], time.monotonic() - t0)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        st = await process_org(tx, org_id, [r["run_id"] for r in results])
        log.info("sync %s: processed %d envelopes in %.1fs", org_id, st.processed, time.monotonic() - t0)
        async with tx(org_id) as conn:
            graph = await run_graph(conn, org_id, vault)
    finally:
        vault.clear()
    pnl = None
    changed = graph["reallocated"] or graph["tier2"]["auto_confirmed"] or graph["tier3"]["auto_confirmed"]
    if recompute and (st.processed or any(r["new"] for r in results) or changed):
        pnl = await recompute(org_id)
    return {"runs": results, "processing": st.as_dict(), "graph": graph, "pnl": pnl}

            return _ok({"organizations": chunk, "meta": {"has_more": more, "after_cursor": str(start + size)}})
        if path == "/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor.json":
            if "cursor" in q:
                start = int(str(q["cursor"]).removeprefix("c"))
            else:
                since = int(q.get("start_time", 0))
                start = next((i for i, t in enumerate(tickets)
                              if _ts(datetime.fromisoformat(t["updated_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))) >= since),
                             len(tickets))
            chunk = tickets[start:start + page]
            ids = {t["id"] for t in chunk}
            end = start + len(chunk)
            return _ok({"tickets": chunk, "metric_sets": [m for m in metric_sets if m["ticket_id"] in ids],
                        "after_cursor": f"c{end}", "end_of_stream": end >= len(tickets)})
        return HttpResponse(404, {}, {"error": f"no sandbox route {path}"})

class SandboxCostExplorer:
    def __init__(self, manifest_text: str, page_size: int = 20):
        w = _world(manifest_text)
        self.page_size = page_size
        self.by_month: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        for c in w["seed"].dataset.cost_lines:
            key = "feature$" + (w["feats"][c.feature_id].key if c.feature_id else "")
            if c.cost_type == "llm":
                parts = [("Amazon Bedrock", c.amount_usd)]
            else:
                ec2 = round(c.amount_usd * 0.7, 2)
                parts = [("Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute", ec2),
                         ("Amazon Relational Database Service", round(c.amount_usd - ec2, 2))]
            for svc, amt in parts:
                self.by_month.setdefault(c.period_month.isoformat(), []).append(
                    {"Keys": [key, svc], "Metrics": {"UnblendedCost": {"Amount": f"{amt:.2f}", "Unit": "USD"}}})

    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        start = kw["TimePeriod"]["Start"]
        groups = self.by_month.get(start, [])
        offset = int(kw.get("NextPageToken") or 0)
        chunk = groups[offset:offset + self.page_size]
        out: dict[str, Any] = {"ResultsByTime": [{"TimePeriod": kw["TimePeriod"], "Groups": chunk, "Estimated": False}]}
        if offset + self.page_size < len(groups):
            out["NextPageToken"] = str(offset + self.page_size)
        return out

"""Zendesk Support (Tickets + Metrics).

Streams
  `organizations`: GET /api/v2/organizations?page[size]=100 (cursor pages), full refresh: domain names
                   drive identity stitching.
  `tickets`: incremental cursor export GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor.json?start_time=...&include=metric_sets,
             then `?cursor=<after_cursor>` until `end_of_stream`. The `after_cursor` is the stream cursor.

Handle time: Zendesk has no native handle time. If `time_field_id` (the Time Tracking app's "total time
spent (sec)" field) is configured it is used; otherwise handle time is estimated as replies × 12 minutes
and the ticket is flagged `handle_time_estimated`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator

from .base import Batch, Connector, SyncCtx, add_months, month_start
from .scrub import scrub_zendesk_org, scrub_zendesk_ticket

MINUTES_PER_REPLY = 12


def handle_minutes(ticket: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, bool]:
    if ticket.get("time_spent_seconds") is not None:
        return max(0, round(ticket["time_spent_seconds"] / 60)), False
    replies = ticket.get("replies") or 1
    return int(replies) * MINUTES_PER_REPLY, True


class ZendeskConnector(Connector):
    kind = "zendesk"
    streams = ("organizations", "tickets")

    def __init__(self, transport, time_field_id: int | None = None):
        super().__init__(transport)
        self.time_field_id = time_field_id

    async def _orgs(self, ctx: SyncCtx) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        params: dict[str, Any] | None = {"page[size]": 100}
        url: str | None = "/api/v2/organizations"
        while url:
            r = await self.t.request("GET", url, params=params)
            envs = [ctx.envelope("zendesk_org", str(o["id"]), o.get("updated_at") or "", scrub_zendesk_org(o))
                    for o in r.body.get("organizations", [])]
            meta = r.body.get("meta") or {}
            if meta.get("has_more"):
                params = {"page[size]": 100, "page[after]": meta.get("after_cursor")}
            else:
                url = None
            yield Batch("organizations", envs, ctx.now().isoformat() if url is None else None)

"""Value attribution: three models, two lenses.

Additive lens (sums to MRR, goes into the ledger):
  engagement  e(a,f) = active_days(a,f) * ln(1 + active_users(a,f))
      Active days, not raw events: a chatty autocomplete event must not outweigh a weekly export.
  usage_weighted   V(f) = sum_a  R(a) * e(a,f) / sum_g e(a,g)          (g over product features)
  tier_gated       for an account on tier T with uplift share u_T:
                   V(f) = sum_a [ u_T * R(a) * e(a,f) / sum_{g gated<=T} e(a,g) ]   if f is gated to T
                        + (1 - u_T) * R(a) * e(a,f) / sum_g e(a,g)
                   If the account used no gated feature, the uplift falls back to usage-weighted.

Counterfactual lens (NOT additive, guards decisions):
  concentration    c(a,f) = active_days(a,f) / distinct_active_days(a)
  churn risk       risk(a,f) = 0                                     if c < 0.10
                             = min(1, c / C*) * proximity * health   otherwise
                   proximity: renewal <= 90d -> 1.0, <= 180d -> 0.8, later/unknown -> 0.6
                   health:    red 1.0, yellow 0.9, green 0.7
  revenue at risk  RaR(f) = sum_a ARR(a) * risk(a,f)
  anchor account   c(a,f) >= C* and ARR(a) >= anchor_min_arr
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

from .types import Account, Feature, OrgSettings, Usage

TIER_RANK = {"free": 0, "starter": 1, "pro": 2, "enterprise": 3}
CONCENTRATION_FLOOR = 0.10
HEALTH_FACTOR = {"red": 1.0, "yellow": 0.9, "green": 0.7}


def engagement(active_days: int, active_users: int) -> float:
    if active_days <= 0 or active_users <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return active_days * math.log1p(active_users)


def renewal_proximity(renewal: date | None, as_of: date) -> float:
    if renewal is None:
        return 0.6
    days = (renewal - as_of).days
    if days <= 90:
        return 1.0
    if days <= 180:
        return 0.8
    return 0.6


def churn_risk(concentration: float, renewal: date | None, health: str, as_of: date,
               threshold: float) -> float:
    if concentration < CONCENTRATION_FLOOR:
        return 0.0
    r = min(1.0, concentration / threshold) * renewal_proximity(renewal, as_of) * HEALTH_FACTOR.get(health, 0.7)
    return round(min(max(r, 0.0), 1.0), 4)

"""Sunset damage signals: turn Sentry webhooks and generic signal posts into per-feature evidence.

Attribution, most explicit first:
    tag    the event carries a `feature` tag (Sentry tag, or `feature` in a generic signal)
    route  the request route matches one of the feature's `api_routes` in features.yaml
    path   a stack frame's file matches one of the feature's `paths` globs
    none   stored for visibility, blocks nothing

Nothing identifying is kept: titles are redacted (emails, long numbers), routes lose their query string
and numeric / uuid segments, stack frames are only used for matching and never stored.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Iterable
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from .manifest import FeatureSpec, glob_specificity, glob_to_regex

FEATURE_TAGS = ("feature", "featureledger.feature", "feature_key")
EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+")
NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\+?\d[\d\s().-]{5,}\d")
ID_SEGMENT = re.compile(r"^(?:\d+|[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F-]{27,}|[0-9a-fA-F]{16,})$")
KINDS = ("error", "deprecated_call")


class SignalError(ValueError):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Signal:
    source: str
    kind: str
    external_id: str
    occurred_at: datetime
    occurrences: int = 1
    title: str | None = None
    route: str | None = None
    feature_tag: str | None = None
    frames: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def redact(s: str | None, limit: int = 200) -> str | None:
    if not s:
        return None
    s = NUM_RE.sub("[number]", EMAIL_RE.sub("[email]", s))
    return " ".join(s.split())[:limit]


def clean_route(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not raw:
        return None
    path = urlparse(raw).path if "://" in raw else raw.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        return None
    return "/".join(":id" if ID_SEGMENT.match(seg) else seg for seg in path.split("/"))[:300]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- generic
def parse_generic(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Signal]:
    """{"signals": [{"id", "kind": "error"|"deprecated_call", "feature"?, "route"?, "path"?, "count"?,
                     "occurred_at"?, "title"?}]}  - one post may carry up to 500 signals."""
    items = payload.get("signals")
    if not isinstance(items, list) or not items:
        raise SignalError("expected a non-empty 'signals' list")
    if len(items) > 500:
        raise SignalError("at most 500 signals per request")
    out = []
    for i, it in enumerate(items):
        if not isinstance(it, dict):
            raise SignalError(f"signals[{i}] is not an object")
        kind = it.get("kind")
        if kind not in KINDS:
            raise SignalError(f"signals[{i}].kind must be one of {KINDS}")
        sid = str(it.get("id") or "").strip()
        if not sid or len(sid) > 200:
            raise SignalError(f"signals[{i}].id is required (your own unique id, max 200 chars)")
        try:
            count = max(1, min(int(it.get("count") or 1), 10_000_000))
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
            raise SignalError(f"signals[{i}].count must be a number") from e
        path = it.get("path")
        out.append(Signal("generic", kind, sid, _when(it.get("occurred_at")), count, redact(it.get("title")),
                          clean_route(it.get("route")), (it.get("feature") or None),
                          (str(path),) if path else ()))
    return out

chunks.text:
"""Engineering effort model: relative per-PR effort, calibrated to real team capacity.

    H_raw(pr) = (0.5 + 1.2 * ln(1 + churn / 20))           size: log-damped, typo ~0.6h
              * (1 + 0.15 * min(review_rounds, 6))          rework from changes-requested cycles
              * (1 + 0.05 * min(files_changed - 1, 20))     coordination across files
              * type_multiplier(kind, priority)             bug/hotfix/incident tax
              + incident_response_hours                     aggregate on-call time (team level)

    churn = additions + 0.5 * deletions   (generated/vendored files are excluded at ingestion)

Calibration ("relative effort, absolute budget"): per team and month
    capacity = headcount * hours_per_engineer_month * allocatable_fraction
    k        = min(capacity / sum(H_raw), calibration_clamp_max)
    H(pr)    = k * H_raw(pr)
Whatever capacity k cannot cover (clamp hit, or a quiet month) is booked as `unattributed`,
so features + overhead + unmapped + unattributed == capacity, always (the conservation invariant).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

from .types import Feature, OrgSettings, Team, WorkItem, WorkKind

TYPE_MULTIPLIER: dict[WorkKind, float] = {
    WorkKind.FEATURE: 1.0,
    WorkKind.CHORE: 0.8,
    WorkKind.BUG: 1.3,
    WorkKind.REVERT: 1.5,
    WorkKind.HOTFIX: 2.0,
    WorkKind.INCIDENT: 2.0,
}
P0_MULTIPLIER = 3.0
BUG_KINDS = {WorkKind.BUG, WorkKind.HOTFIX, WorkKind.INCIDENT, WorkKind.REVERT}


# shares are stored as numeric(6,5); a handful of independently rounded shares can exceed 1 by a few 1e-5
ROUNDING_SLACK = 1e-3


def type_multiplier(kind: WorkKind, priority: str | None) -> float:
    if kind in (WorkKind.HOTFIX, WorkKind.INCIDENT) and (priority or "").upper() == "P0":
        return P0_MULTIPLIER
    return TYPE_MULTIPLIER[kind]

            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(re.escape(c))
            i += 1
    return re.compile("^" + "".join(out) + "$")


def glob_specificity(glob: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    m = re.search(r"[*?]", glob)
    prefix = glob if m is None else glob[: m.start()]
    literal = len(re.sub(r"[*?]", "", glob))
    return len(prefix), literal

"""Feature P&L assembly and health classification.

Per feature f and month m (Contribution view = direct, avoidable cost):
    C_eng     = calibrated_hours(f, m) * eng_hourly_rate
    C_support = sum(handle_minutes)/60 * support_hourly_rate      (tickets mapped to f)
    C_infra   = tagged (fixed) cloud infra for f
    C_ai      = variable AI/LLM token spend for f (Phase 5)
    C_total   = C_eng + C_support + C_infra + C_ai
    GM%       = (V_usage - C_ai - C_infra) / max(V_usage, 1)      gross margin on variable + infra COGS
    Net_ROI   = V_total - C_total
    Efficiency= V_total / max(C_total, 1)
Fully-loaded view adds C_overhead_alloc: the cost of shared-overhead features spread by their
allocation_rule (proportional_usage | proportional_cost | fixed_weights; 'none' = platform line only).

Classification uses a trailing window (default 3 months) and is evaluated in a fixed order
(a Zombie verdict needs at least 2 months of data, because it is a statement about a trend);
the first rule that matches wins, and the reason string records the evidence.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .attribution import MonthAttribution, attribute_month

def classify(f: Feature, window: list[FeaturePnl], s: OrgSettings) -> tuple[FeatureClass, str]:
    """window: oldest -> newest, the newest is the month being classified."""
    cur = window[-1]
    if f.is_shared_overhead:
        return FeatureClass.PLATFORM, "Shared infrastructure, tracked as platform overhead"
    if f.is_regulatory:
        return FeatureClass.MANDATED, "Regulatory/compliance requirement: exempt from sunset"

    if cur.eligible_accounts == 0:
        # No revenue/usage data yet (only Git connected): never call anything a zombie on cost alone.
        return FeatureClass.WATCH, "No usage or revenue data for this month yet: import accounts and usage"
    n = len(window)
    c_avg = sum(r.c_total for r in window) / n
    net = sum(r.v_usage - r.c_total for r in window)
    eng = sum(r.eng_hours for r in window)
    bug_tax = sum(r.bug_hours for r in window) / eng if eng else 0.0
    adoption = cur.adoption
    trend = cur.active_accounts - window[0].active_accounts
    growth = [
        (b.active_accounts - a.active_accounts) / a.active_accounts
        for a, b in zip(window, window[1:]) if a.active_accounts > 0
    ]
    mom = sum(growth) / len(growth) if growth else 0.0
    age = _months_between(f.launched_at, cur.period_month) if f.launched_at else 999

    if adoption < s.anchor_max_adoption and cur.anchor_accounts > 0:
        return FeatureClass.NICHE_ANCHOR, (
            f"Adoption {adoption:.1%} but {cur.anchor_accounts} account(s) ≥${s.anchor_min_arr_usd:,.0f} ARR "
            f"depend on it; ${cur.revenue_at_risk_arr:,.0f} ARR at risk. Do not kill blindly")
    if (n >= 2 and adoption < s.zombie_max_adoption and net < 0 and trend <= 0
            and (bug_tax >= s.zombie_min_bug_tax or c_avg >= s.zombie_min_monthly_cost)):
        return FeatureClass.ZOMBIE, (
            f"Adoption {adoption:.1%}, {n}-mo net ${net:,.0f}, bug tax {bug_tax:.0%}, "
            f"avg cost ${c_avg:,.0f}/mo, usage trend {trend:+d} accounts")
    if (age < s.growth_max_age_months or mom >= s.growth_min_mom_adoption) and cur.c_total >= cur.v_usage:
        return FeatureClass.GROWTH_BET, (
            f"Age {age if age < 999 else 'n/a'} mo, adoption growth {mom:+.0%}/mo, "
            f"investing ${cur.c_total:,.0f} vs ${cur.v_usage:,.0f} attributed")
    if cur.efficiency() >= s.cash_cow_min_efficiency:
        return FeatureClass.CASH_COW, f"Efficiency {cur.efficiency():.1f}x on ${cur.v_usage:,.0f}/mo attributed"
    return FeatureClass.WATCH, (
        f"Efficiency {cur.efficiency():.2f}x, adoption {adoption:.1%}: no rule triggered")


LOW_TIERS = ("free", "starter")

def ai_tier_breakdown(r: FeaturePnl, usage: list, tiers: dict[str, str], attributed: dict[str, float],
                      mrr: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Spread the feature's token spend over plan tiers by usage events (the closest proxy to tokens
    available without per-request metering), next to the revenue the feature earns on each tier."""
    events: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    accounts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    revenue: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    tier_mrr: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    for u in usage:
        if u.events <= 0:
            continue
        t = tiers.get(u.account_id, "unknown")
        events[t] += u.events
        accounts[t] += 1
        revenue[t] += attributed.get(u.account_id, 0.0)
        tier_mrr[t] += mrr.get(u.account_id, 0.0)
    total = sum(events.values())
    if total == 0:
        return {}
    return {t: {"tokens_usd": round(r.c_ai_tokens * events[t] / total, 2), "revenue_usd": round(revenue[t], 2),
                "accounts": accounts[t], "events": events[t], "token_share": round(events[t] / total, 4)}
            for t in sorted(events, key=lambda t: -events[t])}


def detect_margin_bleed(f: Feature, r: FeaturePnl, s: OrgSettings) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    """margin_bleed: a popular feature whose variable AI spend (with infra) leaves too little gross margin.
    Independent of the health class: a Growth Bet can bleed margin too, and that is exactly when to look."""
    if f.is_shared_overhead or r.c_ai_tokens <= 0 or r.eligible_accounts == 0:
        return False, None
    gm = r.gross_margin_pct
    if r.adoption <= s.margin_bleed_min_adoption or gm >= s.margin_bleed_max_gross_margin:
        return False, None
    if r.c_ai_tokens < r.c_infra:      # infra-driven, not token-driven: not this alert
        return False, None
    low = [r.ai_tier_breakdown[t] for t in LOW_TIERS if t in r.ai_tier_breakdown]
    low_tokens = sum(x["tokens_usd"] for x in low)
    low_rev = sum(x["revenue_usd"] for x in low)
    why = (f"Gross margin {gm:.0%} at {r.adoption:.0%} adoption: ${r.c_ai_tokens:,.0f}/mo LLM tokens + "
           f"${r.c_infra:,.0f} infra on ${r.v_usage:,.0f} attributed revenue")
    if low_tokens > 0:
        share = low_tokens / r.c_ai_tokens
        why += f"; free/starter accounts burn {share:.0%} of tokens (${low_tokens:,.0f}) for ${low_rev:,.0f} revenue"
    return True, why

chunks.text:
"""Rate limiting: fixed-window counters, shared through Redis, with an in-process fallback.

Rules (per minute unless noted):

    POST /api/v1/auth/dev-login           30 per client address   (password-less sandbox login)
    GET  /api/v1/auth/oidc/*              30 per client address   (SSO redirects / callbacks)
    POST /api/v1/demo/launch|switch-role  30 per client address   (anonymous demo sessions)
    POST /api/v1/webhooks/*             1200 per client address   (vendors retry in bursts)
    everything else under /api/v1       1200 per session token, or per address when anonymous
    POST /api/v1/demo/reset               once per DEMO_RESET_COOLDOWN_S for the whole demo (in the route)

Behind the dashboard every browser call reaches the API from the Next.js server, so the client address is
taken from X-Forwarded-For, TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS entries from the right (1 = Next.js only, 2 = a load
balancer in front of it). Keep the API itself off the public internet, or that header can be forged.

If Redis is unreachable the limiter keeps counting in process memory (per worker) and retries Redis after
30 s: a Redis outage weakens the limits, it never blocks sign-in.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.ratelimit")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rule:
    name: str
    limit: int
    window_s: int
    by_session: bool = False


LOGIN = Rule("login", 30, 60)
SSO = Rule("sso", 30, 60)
DEMO_SESSION = Rule("demo-session", 30, 60)
WEBHOOK = Rule("webhook", 1200, 60)
API = Rule("api", 1200, 60, by_session=True)


def rule_for(method: str, path: str) -> Rule | None:
    if not path.startswith("/api/v1/"):
        return None                                   # /health, /docs
    if method == "POST" and path == "/api/v1/auth/dev-login":
        return LOGIN
    if path.startswith("/api/v1/auth/oidc/"):
        return SSO
    if method == "POST" and path in ("/api/v1/demo/launch", "/api/v1/demo/switch-role"):
        return DEMO_SESSION
    if method == "POST" and path.startswith("/api/v1/webhooks/"):
        return WEBHOOK
    return API

from redis.asyncio import Redis
            except ImportError:
                log.warning("rate limiter: redis package not installed; counting in process memory")
                self.redis_url = None
                return None
            self._redis = Redis.from_url(self.redis_url, socket_connect_timeout=0.25, socket_timeout=0.25)
        return self._redis

    async def hit(self, key: str, limit: int, window_s: int) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        """-> (allowed, seconds until the window resets)."""
        now = time.time()
        start = now - (now % window_s)
        reset = start + window_s
        r = await self._client()
        n = None
        if r is not None:
            k = f"{self.prefix}{key}:{int(start)}"
            try:
                async with r.pipeline(transaction=True) as p:
                    p.incr(k)
                    p.expire(k, window_s + 1)
                    n = (await p.execute())[0]
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - any Redis problem: fall back, retry later
                if self._redis_down_until < now:
                    log.warning("rate limiter: Redis unavailable (%s); counting in process memory", e)
                self._redis_down_until = now + 30
        if n is None:
            n, reset = self.memory.hit(key, window_s, now)
        return n <= limit, max(1, int(reset - now + 0.999))

    async def cooldown(self, key: str, seconds: int) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        """At most once per `seconds`, measured from the last allowed call. -> (allowed, seconds to wait)."""
        now = time.time()
        k = f"{self.prefix}cd:{key}"
        r = await self._client()
        if r is not None:
            try:
                if await r.set(k, "1", nx=True, ex=seconds):
                    return True, 0
                return False, max(1, int(await r.ttl(k) or seconds))
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                if self._redis_down_until < now:
                    log.warning("rate limiter: Redis unavailable (%s); counting in process memory", e)
                self._redis_down_until = now + 30
        until = self._cooldowns.get(k, 0.0)
        if until > now:
            return False, max(1, int(until - now + 0.999))
        self._cooldowns[k] = now + seconds
        return True, 0


_limiter: RateLimiter | None = None

"""What-If Sunset Simulator.

For a set S of features over a trailing window W (default 3 months):
    reclaimed_hours/mo  = avg_W(eng_hours) * (1 - residual)          residual = 10% (on-call, migration tail)
    avoidable_cost/mo   = avg_W(C_eng) * (1 - residual) + avg_W(C_support) + avg_W(C_infra)
    expected_arr_loss   = sum_accounts ARR * max_f churn_risk(a,f) * (1 - migration_success)
                          (an account hit by two sunset features is counted once, at its highest risk)
    net_annual_impact   = 12 * avoidable_cost/mo - expected_arr_loss - one_off_migration_cost
    fte_reclaimed       = reclaimed_hours / (hours_per_engineer_month * allocatable_fraction)
Shared overhead is never "reclaimed": removing a feature does not remove auth/ or the database.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

from .pnl import FeaturePnl
from .types import OrgSettings

RESIDUAL = 0.10


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AccountExposure:
    account_id: str
    name: str
    arr_usd: float
    churn_risk: float
    feature_keys: tuple[str, ...]


def simulate(
    rows_by_feature: dict[str, list[FeaturePnl]],
    exposures: list[tuple[str, str, float, float, str]],  # (account_id, name, arr, churn_risk, feature_key)
    settings: OrgSettings,
    migration_success: float = 0.7,
    one_off_migration_cost: float = 0.0,
) -> dict:
    if not 0 <= migration_success <= 1:
        raise ValueError("migration_success must be within [0, 1]")
    per_feature = []
    hours = cost = 0.0
    for key, rows in rows_by_feature.items():
        n = max(len(rows), 1)
        h = sum(r.eng_hours for r in rows) / n * (1 - RESIDUAL)
        c = (sum(r.c_eng for r in rows) / n * (1 - RESIDUAL)
             + sum(r.c_support for r in rows) / n + sum(r.c_infra for r in rows) / n)
        v = sum(r.v_usage for r in rows) / n
        hours += h
        cost += c
        per_feature.append({"feature_key": key, "reclaimed_hours_month": round(h, 1),
                            "avoidable_cost_month": round(c, 2), "attributed_mrr": round(v, 2)})

        "one_off_migration_cost": round(one_off_migration_cost, 2),
        "net_annual_impact": round(cost * 12 - expected_loss - one_off_migration_cost, 2),
        "migration_success_assumed": migration_success,
        "accounts": sorted(
            ({"account_id": a.account_id, "name": a.name, "arr_usd": a.arr_usd,
              "churn_risk": a.churn_risk, "features": list(a.feature_keys)} for a in accts.values()),
            key=lambda x: -x["arr_usd"]),
    }


def trailing_months(end: date, n: int) -> list[date]:
    out, y, m = [], end.year, end.month
    for _ in range(n):
        out.append(date(y, m, 1))
        m -= 1
        if m == 0:
            y, m = y - 1, 12
    return sorted(out)

"""Safe Sunset orchestrator: a guarded state machine.

    candidate_for_sunset -> blast_radius_checked -> customer_outreach -> canary_dark_launch
        -> dead_code_pr_opened -> archived
    rollback:  canary_dark_launch | dead_code_pr_opened -> customer_outreach  (flag re-enabled)
    cancel:    any non-terminal state -> cancelled

Scream-test evidence that blocks progress: 'on' flag evaluations, support tickets, and damage signals
(production errors and calls to the feature's deprecated API routes, app/core/damage.py).

Every transition is a pure function of (plan, context) -> TransitionResult, so the API layer only
persists the result + an audit row. Guards encode the "never delete blindly" rules.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any


class SunsetState(str, Enum):
    CANDIDATE = "candidate_for_sunset"
    BLAST_RADIUS_CHECKED = "blast_radius_checked"
    CUSTOMER_OUTREACH = "customer_outreach"
    CANARY_DARK_LAUNCH = "canary_dark_launch"
    DEAD_CODE_PR_OPENED = "dead_code_pr_opened"
    ARCHIVED = "archived"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"


ORDER = [SunsetState.CANDIDATE, SunsetState.BLAST_RADIUS_CHECKED, SunsetState.CUSTOMER_OUTREACH,
         SunsetState.CANARY_DARK_LAUNCH, SunsetState.DEAD_CODE_PR_OPENED, SunsetState.ARCHIVED]
TERMINAL = {SunsetState.ARCHIVED, SunsetState.CANCELLED}
ROLLBACK_FROM = {SunsetState.CANARY_DARK_LAUNCH, SunsetState.DEAD_CODE_PR_OPENED}
HIGH_RISK = 0.5           # churn_risk at/above which CS sign-off is mandatory
OUTREACH_GRACE_DAYS = 14  # unacknowledged accounts block the canary for this long


class TransitionError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code


@dataclass
class PlanView:
    state: SunsetState
    feature_is_regulatory: bool
    flag_key: str | None
    scream_test_days: int

"""Evidence generators for the Safe Sunset pipeline (pure functions).

* blast_radius   - who still imports the feature's code (static import graph, metadata only)
* impact_dossier - paying accounts that used it in the lookback window, ARR-sorted, with a drafted
                   migration email per account for Customer Success to edit and send
* cleanup_pr     - outline of the dead-code PR: paths, routes, flag checks, tests, call sites
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from .manifest import FeatureSpec, Manifest, glob_to_regex


def _in_feature(path: str, spec: FeatureSpec) -> bool:
    return any(glob_to_regex(g).match(path) for g in spec.paths)


def blast_radius(spec: FeatureSpec, manifest: Manifest, edges: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """edges: (from_path, to_path) import edges across the org's repos."""
    inbound: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for src, dst in edges:
        if _in_feature(dst, spec) and not _in_feature(src, spec):
            inbound[src].add(dst)
    refs = []
    for src in sorted(inbound):
        refs.append({
            "from_path": src,
            "owner_feature": manifest.owner_of(src) or "unmapped",
            "imports": sorted(inbound[src]),
            "acknowledged": False,
        })
    by_owner: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for r in refs:
        by_owner[r["owner_feature"]] += 1
    return {
        "feature": spec.key,
        "inbound_references": refs,
        "inbound_count": len(refs),
        "by_owner_feature": dict(sorted(by_owner.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
        "api_routes": list(spec.api_routes),
        "flag_key": spec.flag_key,
        "risk": "low" if not refs else ("medium" if len(refs) <= 5 else "high"),
    }

def cleanup_pr_outline(spec: FeatureSpec, br: dict[str, Any], known_files: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    owned = sorted(p for p in known_files if _in_feature(p, spec))
    tests = [p for p in owned if any(t in p for t in ("/test", "test_", ".test.", ".spec.", "__tests__"))]
    code = [p for p in owned if p not in tests]
    callers = [r["from_path"] for r in br.get("inbound_references", [])]
    title = f"chore(sunset): remove {spec.name} ({spec.key})"
    lines = [
        f"Removes **{spec.name}** after a clean scream test. Generated by FeatureLedger.",
        "",
        "### Delete",
        *[f"- [ ] `{p}`" for p in code],
        "",
        "### Delete tests",
        *([f"- [ ] `{p}`" for p in tests] or ["- [ ] (no tests found under the feature's paths)"]),
        "",
        "### Edit call sites (remove imports / dead branches)",
        *([f"- [ ] `{p}`" for p in callers] or ["- [ ] none: no inbound imports"]),
        "",
        "### Routes",
        *([f"- [ ] remove handler + OpenAPI entry for `{r}`" for r in spec.api_routes] or ["- [ ] none"]),
        "",
        "### Feature flag",
        (f"- [ ] remove all `{spec.flag_key}` checks, then archive the flag in the flag provider"
         if spec.flag_key else "- [ ] none"),
        "",
        "### Manifest",
        f"- [ ] delete the `{spec.key}` entry from `features.yaml` (FeatureLedger archives the feature on merge)",
    ]
    return {
        "title": title,
        "branch": f"featureledger/sunset-{spec.key}",
        "body_markdown": "\n".join(lines),
        "files_to_delete": code + tests,
        "files_to_edit": callers,
        "routes_to_remove": list(spec.api_routes),
        "flag_key": spec.flag_key,
    }

chunks.text:
"""asyncpg pool + tenant-scoped transactions.

Every request runs inside `org_tx(org_id)`, which sets `app.org_id` for the transaction only
(`set_config(..., true)`), so Row-Level Security filters every statement, and a pooled connection
can never carry one tenant's id into another request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import AsyncIterator

import asyncpg

from .config import config

_pool: asyncpg.Pool | None = None


async def _init_conn(conn: asyncpg.Connection) -> None:
    for typ in ("json", "jsonb"):
        await conn.set_type_codec(typ, encoder=json.dumps, decoder=json.loads, schema="pg_catalog")
    # pgvector: bind and read vectors as their text form '[0.1,0.2,...]' (no extra client library)
    if await conn.fetchval("SELECT to_regtype('public.vector') IS NOT NULL"):
        await conn.set_type_codec("vector", encoder=str, decoder=str, schema="public", format="text")


async def init_pool(dsn: str | None = None) -> asyncpg.Pool:
    global _pool
    if _pool is None:
        # jit=off: short OLTP statements (and asyncpg's type introspection) must not pay LLVM compile time
        _pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(dsn or config.database_url, min_size=1, max_size=10, init=_init_conn,
                                          server_settings={"jit": "off"})
    return _pool


async def close_pool() -> None:
    global _pool
    if _pool is not None:
        await _pool.close()
        _pool = None


@asynccontextmanager
async def org_tx(org_id: str) -> AsyncIterator[asyncpg.Connection]:
    pool = await init_pool()
    async with pool.acquire() as conn:
        async with conn.transaction():
            await conn.execute("SELECT set_config('app.org_id', $1, true)", str(org_id))
            yield conn


async def resolve_org(slug: str) -> str | None:
    pool = await init_pool()
    async with pool.acquire() as conn:
        v = await conn.fetchval("SELECT resolve_org_slug($1)", slug)
    return str(v) if v else None

async def auth_call(fn: str, *args) -> dict | None:
    """Call one of the pre-tenant SECURITY DEFINER auth functions (0006); returns one user row or None."""
    pool = await init_pool()
    placeholders = ", ".join(f"${i + 1}" for i in range(len(args)))

chunks.text:
"""Live demo org (DEMO_MODE=true): "Acme Cloud", the seed company re-keyed into its own tenant.

The demo org is a normal tenant behind RLS, with three extra properties:
  * organizations.is_demo = true, which is the only kind of org /api/v1/demo/reset may delete;
  * every id is a deterministic uuid5 of the seed's id under DEMO_NS, so a reset restores the very same
    plans, users and integration ids (open browser tabs keep working);
  * flags, cleanup PRs, PR comments and Slack always use sandbox providers in this org, whatever the
    deployment is configured with (app/execution/orchestrator.providers_for, app/db.org_is_demo).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
import time
import uuid

from .config import config

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.demo")
DEMO_NS = uuid.UUID("2d0c3d6e-6a0f-4c55-9d44-5ad3c0de0a01")
UUID_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")
DEMO_LABEL = "Launch Live Demo ({name} — {engineers} Engineers)"
ORPHAN_TABLES_SQL = """
    SELECT c.relname FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = c.oid AND a.attname = 'org_id'
     WHERE c.relkind IN ('r', 'p') AND c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND NOT c.relispartition
       AND c.relname <> 'organizations'
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint k WHERE k.conrelid = c.oid AND k.contype = 'f'
                                                      AND k.confrelid = 'organizations'::regclass)"""


def demo_id(seed_id: str) -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid5(DEMO_NS, seed_id))


def demo_seed_sql(seed_sql: str, slug: str, name: str) -> str:
    """Re-key the deterministic seed into the demo tenant (full data set: no connector sync needed)."""
    sql = UUID_RE.sub(lambda m: demo_id(m.group(0)), seed_sql)
    sql = sql.replace(",'Northwind Cloud','northwind')", f",'{name.replace(chr(39), chr(39) * 2)}','{slug}')")
    sql = sql.replace("@northwind.io", "@acme-cloud.demo").replace("northwind/app", "acme/app")
    sql = sql.replace("GitHub · northwind", "GitHub · acme")
    # sandbox AWS Cost Explorer owns all cost lines in the demo, so a "Trigger Sync" rebuilds instead of adding
    sql = sql.replace("'openai_usage'", "'aws_cost_explorer'")
    return "\n".join(ln for ln in sql.splitlines() if ln.strip() not in ("BEGIN;", "COMMIT;"))


async def reset_demo(dsn: str | None = None, converge_now: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Delete the demo org (only if it is flagged is_demo) and seed it again; then compute its P&L."""
    import asyncpg
    from .db import _init_conn
    from .jobs.compute_pnl import recompute_org
    from .seed.generate import build
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    seed = build(config.manifest_path.read_text())
    org_id = demo_id(seed.org_id)
    sql = demo_seed_sql(seed.sql, config.demo_org_slug, config.demo_org_name)
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(dsn or config.admin_database_url, server_settings={"jit": "off"})
    try:
        await _init_conn(conn)
        async with conn.transaction():
            await conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('featureledger:demo-reset'))")

chunks.title: demo.py › converge

seed = build(config.manifest_path.read_text())
    org_id = demo_id(seed.org_id)
    sql = demo_seed_sql(seed.sql, config.demo_org_slug, config.demo_org_name)
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(dsn or config.admin_database_url, server_settings={"jit": "off"})
    try:
        await _init_conn(conn)
        async with conn.transaction():
            await conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('featureledger:demo-reset'))")
            for r in await conn.fetch("SELECT id, is_demo FROM organizations WHERE slug = $1 OR id = $2::uuid",
                                      config.demo_org_slug, org_id):
                if not r["is_demo"]:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"organization {config.demo_org_slug!r} is a real tenant; refusing to reset it")
                await conn.execute("SELECT set_config('featureledger.purge_org', $1, true)", str(r["id"]))
                await conn.execute("DELETE FROM sunset_audit_logs WHERE org_id = $1", r["id"])
                # partitioned fact tables carry org_id without a foreign key: the cascade cannot reach them
                for t in await conn.fetch(ORPHAN_TABLES_SQL):
                    await conn.execute(f'DELETE FROM "{t["relname"]}" WHERE org_id = $1', r["id"])
                await conn.execute("DELETE FROM organizations WHERE id = $1", r["id"])
            await conn.execute(sql)
            await conn.execute("UPDATE organizations SET is_demo = true WHERE id = $1::uuid", org_id)
            await conn.execute("""UPDATE integrations SET sandbox = true, status = 'active', last_error = NULL
                                   WHERE org_id = $1::uuid AND kind <> 'github'""", org_id)
        # ~30k rows were just bulk-loaded: without fresh statistics the planner picks nested loops and
        # Tier 3's subject collection took ~6 minutes instead of well under a second
        await conn.execute("ANALYZE")
    finally:
        await conn.close()
    converged = await converge(org_id) if converge_now else {}
    pnl = converged.get("pnl") or await recompute_org(org_id)   # app role + RLS, never the admin connection
    took = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1)
    log.info("demo org %s reset in %ss: %s", config.demo_org_slug, took, pnl.get("classes"))
    return {"org_id": org_id, "slug": config.demo_org_slug, "seconds": took, "pnl": pnl,
            "graph": {k: converged["graph"][k] for k in ("tier2", "tier3")} if converged.get("graph") else None}


async def converge(org_id: str) -> dict:
    """Run one in-process sandbox sync + Feature Graph pass so the demo starts at its steady state.

    The seed SQL is the *pre-inference* state: it carries the facts but not what Tier 2 (code clusters) and
    Tier 3 (ticket text) infer on the first sync, nor the Jira issues and the `__unresolved__` usage account.
    Without this step the visitor's first "Trigger Sync" moved ~155 engineering hours and ~79 tickets onto
    features (+0.4% monthly cost). After it, any further sync over unchanged fixtures changes nothing.
    """
    from .connectors.ratelimit import MemoryBucketStore
    from .connectors.runner import sync_org
    from .db import org_tx
    from .jobs.compute_pnl import recompute_org
    async with org_tx(org_id) as conn:
        integs = [dict(r) for r in await conn.fetch("""SELECT id, kind::text AS kind, config, sandbox FROM integrations
                                                       WHERE status <> 'disabled' AND kind <> 'github' AND sandbox""")]
    if not integs:
        return {}
    return await sync_org(org_tx, org_id, integs, "manual", MemoryBucketStore(), recompute_org)

chunks.text:
"""Safe Sunset execution: the side effects behind each guarded transition.

The pure state machine (app/core/sunset.py) decides *whether* a plan may move. This module makes the
move real, inside the same database transaction as the state change, and fails closed: if a flag
provider or GitHub call fails, the transaction rolls back and the plan stays where it was.

    customer_outreach  -> canary_dark_launch   flag -> zero_usage_off (on only for accounts with usage in 90 d)
    canary (promote)                            flag -> fully_off; the scream-test clock starts
    canary_dark_launch -> dead_code_pr_opened   evaluations re-pulled, guards re-checked, cleanup PR opened
    dead_code_pr_opened -> archived             PR merge webhook (or an admin); feature archived
    rollback / cancel from canary or PR         flag -> fully_on, cleanup PR closed, rollback_count + 1
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any

from ..auth.session import Principal
from ..cleanup.change import build_cleanup_change
from ..cleanup.github import CleanupPRProvider, CleanupProviderError, get_cleanup_provider
from ..config import config
from ..core.manifest import ManifestError, parse_manifest
from ..core.sunset import ROLLBACK_FROM, PlanView, SunsetState, TransitionResult, advance
from ..core.sunset_artifacts import blast_radius
from ..flags.base import EvalBucket, FlagProvider, FlagProviderError, FlagState
from ..flags.registry import get_flag_provider

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.sunset")

PLAN_SQL = """
    SELECT p.*, f.key AS feature_key, f.name AS feature_name, f.flag_key, f.is_regulatory, f.is_shared_overhead,
           f.metadata AS feature_metadata
      FROM sunset_plans p JOIN features f ON f.id = p.feature_id"""


class ExecutionError(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, status: int = 502):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code, self.status = code, status


class PlanNotFound(LookupError):

def view(p) -> PlanView:
    return PlanView(state=SunsetState(p["state"]), feature_is_regulatory=p["is_regulatory"], flag_key=p["flag_key"],
                    scream_test_days=p["scream_test_days"], state_entered_at=p["state_entered_at"],

async def load(conn, plan_id, for_update: bool = False):
    try:
        p = await conn.fetchrow(PLAN_SQL + " WHERE p.id = $1::uuid" + (" FOR UPDATE OF p" if for_update else ""),
                                str(plan_id))
    except Exception as e:   # malformed uuid
        if "invalid input syntax for type uuid" in str(e):
            raise PlanNotFound(plan_id) from e
        raise
    if not p:
        raise PlanNotFound(plan_id)
    return p


async def persist(conn, org: str, p, res: TransitionResult, note: dict[str, Any], actor: Principal | None,
                  system: str | None = None):
    """Write the transition + its audit row. `res.updates` already carries execution results."""
    u = res.updates
    entered = datetime.now(timezone.utc) if res.to_state != res.from_state or res.action == "canary_promote" \
        else p["state_entered_at"]
    await conn.execute("""
        UPDATE sunset_plans SET state = $2::sunset_state, canary_phase = $3,
               blast_radius = coalesce($4, blast_radius), impact_dossier = coalesce($5, impact_dossier),
               canary = coalesce($6, canary), cleanup_pr = coalesce($7, cleanup_pr),
               state_entered_at = $8, updated_at = now(), version = version + 1,
               rollback_count = rollback_count + $9
         WHERE id = $1""", p["id"], res.to_state.value,
        u["canary_phase"] if "canary_phase" in u else p["canary_phase"],
        u.get("blast_radius"), u.get("impact_dossier"), u.get("canary"), u.get("cleanup_pr"), entered,
        1 if res.action == "rollback" else 0)
    if res.to_state is SunsetState.ARCHIVED:
        # freeze what the sunset reclaimed before the feature leaves the ledger (executive digest reads it)
        await conn.execute("UPDATE sunset_plans SET reclaimed = $2 WHERE id = $1", p["id"],
                           await reclaimed_snapshot(conn, p["feature_id"]))
        await conn.execute("UPDATE features SET status = 'archived', updated_at = now() WHERE id = $1", p["feature_id"])
    elif res.to_state is SunsetState.CANCELLED:
        await conn.execute("UPDATE features SET status = 'active', updated_at = now() WHERE id = $1", p["feature_id"])
    elif res.to_state in (SunsetState.CANARY_DARK_LAUNCH, SunsetState.DEAD_CODE_PR_OPENED):
        await conn.execute("UPDATE features SET status = 'sunsetting' WHERE id = $1", p["feature_id"])
    elif res.action == "rollback":
        await conn.execute("UPDATE features SET status = 'candidate_for_sunset' WHERE id = $1", p["feature_id"])
    await audit(conn, org, p["id"], res.from_state.value, res.to_state.value, res.action,
                {**note, **({"flag_action": u["flag_action"]} if "flag_action" in u else {})}, actor, system)
    return await load(conn, p["id"])
